verevonRelevance: Verevon has reattach_skill and a skills character budget; explicit pruned markers plus a verbatim re-list are a sturdier contract than silent drops.

name: Memory-aware compaction handoff
what: Compaction knows about memory: providers can feed insights into the summary prompt, the summary states that memory remains authoritative, and the memory block is reloaded from disk when the prompt is rebuilt.
how: compress(memory_context=...) receives on_pre_compress output via sanitize_memory_context (force redaction, 6,000 char cap with 4,000 head and 1,500 tail); SUMMARY_PREFIX asserts MEMORY.md/USER.md are always authoritative; invalidate_system_prompt reloads MEMORY.md/USER.md so this session writes become visible after compaction.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already injects a compaction memory directive (fetch_compaction_memory_directive); the sanitize-and-cap step and the "memory is authoritative" clause are small adds.

name: Pluggable ContextEngine (lossless engines such as LCM)
what: The compaction strategy can be replaced by a plugin engine selected in config; the engine decides when to compact, how, and may expose its own tools such as grep over archived context.
how: ContextEngine ABC (agent/context_engine.py) requires name, update_from_response(usage), should_compress, should_compress_info, compress(messages, current_tokens, focus_topic, force, memory_context) and maintains token state attributes; context.engine selects plugins/context_engine/<name>; plugin engines are never auto-activated. Host guards (user-turn anchor, last-reply anchor) are applied at the commit boundary for every engine.
verevonRelevance: Not needed now; shows the seam for swapping summary versus lossless compaction behind one trait.

name: Compaction recall eval harness (recall accuracy versus tokens retained)
what: Compaction policies are scored by what a fresh model can still answer from only the post-compaction context, not by tokens saved.
how: evals/compaction/runner.py takes a real long transcript, generates and caches a bank of factual questions from the region that compaction will summarize, runs each policy (current, lean, codex-style, aggressive tail, or a Jev decision-model arm), asks a fresh LLM, judges against gold and emits a scorecard of recall versus tokens. scripts/ rebuild transcripts from session lineages (copy the DB first, dedupe rotation copies by content hash, resolve prompts through system_prompts) and render an HTML before/after report; test_region_scoping.py plants sentinels to prove the summarizer only sees the middle region.
verevonRelevance: Verevon eval-lab-py already ported this (cases/compaction); the lineage-reconstruction scripts and the region-scoping tripwire are the unported parts.
notes: Transcripts are intentionally not committed (real session data). Peer inventories report no compaction eval harness (Claude: none found; Codex: developer scripts only).

name: A/B eval methodology for prompt and tool-schema diets (session_search, prefix re-diet)
what: Changes to tool schemas or the fixed prompt prefix are validated with live A/B runs where only one file differs, seeded deterministic data and programmatic oracles, run on weak and mid models three times each.
how: evals/session_search_schema/runner.py extracts tools/session_search_tool.py from two git refs and runs six tasks (discover, forced scroll, broaden, link emission, profile link, browse) against a seeded session DB with oracles; metrics include pass, calls, malformed calls, first-call prompt tokens and wall time; rules require 3 reps, identical denominators and one retry for provider noise. evals/prefix_rediet runs real AIAgents from two checkouts with scripted browser and vault stubs to prove deferred tools are still found after the prompt diet (schema diet 1,570 to 695 tokens/call).
verevonRelevance: Adopt for any Verevon change to tool descriptions or system preambles; weak models are the sensitive signal.
notes: Hermes calls this "hermesbench discipline".

name: Post-mortem forensics for cost, cache behaviour and tool friction
what: Scripts recompute observed (not modeled) figures from a copy of the session database and logs: where money went, cache hit ratios, delegation timeouts, tool-call friction and /goal loop behaviour.
how: evals/postmortem/forensics (tokens, logcalls, delegation, tools, goal_loop, rework) read state_copy.db and rotated agent.log files with no model calls; a reference run reports 1,394 sessions and about $19.3k with cache write/read/output buckets, p50 prompt 229k tokens and 93.9% hit ratio; live_ab and review_probes exercise real code paths against fake providers. Everything is labeled OBSERVED or MODELED.
verevonRelevance: Verevon cost-core could run an equivalent "where did the tokens go" report per org, separating learning, compaction and main-loop spend.
notes: Strong evidence culture; but no eval measures whether learned skills or memories improve task outcomes.

name: Gap: no outcome eval for the learning loop itself
what: The repo evaluates compaction recall, tool schemas and cost, but no harness measures whether memories and skills written by the review actually improve later tasks.
how: evals/ has no background_review, curator or memory-quality harness; coverage is 29 unit-test files for background review/curator (mechanics, guards, cost, cache parity) plus reuse_after_patch counters and opt-in aggregate metrics as indirect signals.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has implicit-dissatisfaction and explicit-feedback signals and calibration rows; building a held-out "did learned skills help" eval on top would put Verevon ahead.
notes: Inference from absence in evals/ and tests/ listings (grep for background_review/curator/memory_tool in evals found only incidental hits).

name: Closed-enum, bucketed, opt-in telemetry for the learning loop
what: Memory operations, curator runs and delegation fan-outs are recorded as aggregate metrics with fixed vocabularies and count buckets, never content, and only inside recorded consent windows.
how: shared_metrics_loop.record_builtin_memory_call(action, operations, outcome, failure_class) maps raw values to closed enums in shared_metrics_contract (MEMORY_OP_FAILURE_CLASSES has 20 values; MEMORY_OP_ORIGINS background_review|foreground; CURATOR_OUTCOMES; COUNT_BUCKETS for archived/created/merged/patched). Recording is a no-op unless shared metrics are enabled for the profile (telemetry.shared_metrics.enabled and send default false) and never raises into callers; packages are sent only if the whole period lies within consent windows.
verevonRelevance: Privacy-by-construction telemetry (closed enums, buckets, consent windows) fits Verevon ZDR and GDPR posture and can measure learning health without reading content.

name: Trajectory export and private trace upload
what: Sessions can be exported as ShareGPT-style trajectories (completed and failed files) for training and debugging, or uploaded as private Hugging Face agent traces in Claude Code JSONL shape with forced secret redaction.
how: agent/trajectory.save_trajectory appends JSONL under a file lock; batch_runner.py produces per-batch outputs with tool stats and checkpoint resume; agent/trace_upload converts OpenAI-format messages to the Claude Code JSONL shape, creates the dataset private, redacts every text body with force=True and refuses upload if redaction fails.
verevonRelevance: Verevon trajectory.rs is an in-memory ring buffer; a persisted, redacted, org-scoped export is the missing half, but Hermes confirms trajectories are not wired to the online learner.
notes: Corroborates the earlier Verevon note that background_review/curator are not a fine-tuning pipeline.

name: Negative finding: no implicit-feedback or user-model learning in core
what: Hermes core does not collect regenerate/edit/correction signals or build a quantitative user model; its only sentiment detector is a cosmetic regex for affection, and learning from corrections relies on the review fork reading the transcript.
how: agent/reactions.detect_reaction matches gratitude/love words and hearts to trigger pet and heart animations (token free, never touches the conversation). The review prompts list frustration phrases ("stop doing X", "too verbose") as first-class skill signals. USER.md is the only built-in user model (1,375 chars). Embeddings or vector retrieval are absent from core (grep over agent, tools, hermes_state*, cron).
verevonRelevance: Verevon is ahead here: implicit dissatisfaction signals with Wilson-bounded skill quarantine and calibration rows have no Hermes equivalent.
notes: Absence claim based on greps; semantic recall and user modeling exist only through external providers (Honcho etc.).

name: Cron jobs as agent runs: scripts, skills, context chaining and multi-platform delivery
what: Users and the agent itself schedule recurring or one-shot agent runs (durations, "every monday 9am", 5-field cron, ISO instants) that load skills, run a data-collection script first, chain the previous job output, run in a given working directory and deliver to one or more channels.
how: cron/jobs.py create_job fields: prompt, schedule, repeat, deliver (origin/local/platform), skills (list), model/provider/base_url, script (stdout injected into the prompt; with no_agent=True the script is the whole job), monitor_script/monitor_url, context_from (job ids; latest non-silent output injected, 8,000 chars cap), enabled_toolsets, workdir (loads AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md), attach_to_session, reasoning_effort, failure_deliver, paused, pinned, interpreter. Jobs live in jobs.json with atomic writes; the agent uses a cronjob_manage tool, users use hermes cron or /cron; a dashboard page and /api/jobs exist.
verevonRelevance: Verevon scheduled runs are one no-tool 1,024-token call with no delivery (baseline); this is the feature-complete reference for what a scheduled run should be able to do.
notes: Quality 5 for execution depth. Peers per the audit-3 inventories: Claude desktop has scheduled tasks (CCD and Cowork, with watcher history and approved permissions), Codex has local automations with inbox items, Cursor has an automations UI with a webhook panel, Manus has scheduled tasks and triggers, DeepSeek has a schedule package, T3 Code none; none of those inventories shows monitor hashing, wake gates or notepads.

name: Monitor-mode cron: hash-suppressed change detection before any LLM call
what: A cron job can attach a cheap source (script or URL). The agent only runs when the source output changed, and when it does it receives a capped diff of what changed.
how: cron/monitor.py hashes the exact UTF-8 bytes of the monitor output (SHA-256, no normalization) and compares with the hash of the last agent-triggering tick: unchanged means a silent no_change run (no LLM); changed or first run injects a "MONITOR CHANGE DETECTED" block with a unified diff capped at 4,000 chars plus new output capped at 8,000; source failure is an error and never counts as a change and leaves the stored hash untouched; monitor_url uses a bounded GET (256 KiB, 30 s). State: monitor_state in jobs.json plus monitor_last_output.txt under the job output directory.
verevonRelevance: Verevon watches (capability-core cron/tasks/watches) could use zero-token change detection before waking a model, which is a major cost lever for monitoring use cases.

name: Wake gate and silent sentinel to avoid pointless runs and messages
what: A pre-run script can print {"wakeAgent": false} to skip the model entirely, and an agent run that has nothing to report replies [SILENT] so no message is delivered.
how: _parse_wake_gate reads the last non-empty stdout line as JSON and skips the agent only when wakeAgent is explicitly false (any other output wakes normally). SILENT_MARKER = "[SILENT]" is recognised as whole response, first line or last line, plus bracketless SILENT / NO_REPLY variants; blueprint prompts and the self-context intro ("avoid repeating what was already reported") use it for continuity.
verevonRelevance: Needed for any Verevon scheduled briefing or watcher so that "nothing new" costs nothing and sends nothing.

name: Per-job durable notepad (cursors and watermarks)
what: Each cron job has a small key-value notepad that persists across wake-ups and is injected into the prompt, so recurring jobs can remember what they already processed.
how: cron/notepad.py stores (job_id, key, value, updated_at) in cron/notepad.db with caps of 16 KB per value, 128-char keys and 64 KB per job; oversized writes raise and leave the store untouched; the write path is the CLI (hermes cron notepad <job> set) via the terminal tool, deliberately not a model tool.
verevonRelevance: A bounded per-task state slot is an easy way to give Verevon scheduled tasks continuity without a full memory system.
notes: Keeping the write path off the model tool surface preserves the narrow-waist rule.

name: At-most-once scheduling, execution ledger, incidents and quota holds
what: Scheduled work is accounted for exactly: missed slots are recovered once, crashes cannot double-fire, failures are grouped into acknowledgeable incidents, and jobs park themselves when a provider usage window is known to be closed.
how: tick() advances next_run_at before dispatch and stamps pending_slot in the same save; cron/occurrences restores a slot once if its owner is dead and the executions ledger (SQLite, scheduled_instant, immutable terminal states, 1,000 terminal rows kept) blocks a second fire; catch-up window is half the period clamped to 120 s - 2 h; per-home tick lock; idle-based inactivity watchdog (default 600 s) interrupts stalled sessions. cron/incidents groups failures by (job_id, normalized error signature) with detected, alerted and closed states and repeat-alert throttling; cron/quota_hold parses "retry after N s" from rate-limited auth errors and parks next_run_at past the recovery boundary (+60 s slack).
verevonRelevance: Verevon cron sweeper to Temporal ScheduledRunSupervision already gives durability; the incident signature dedup and quota-hold parking are concrete reliability features to add.
notes: Multi-profile scoping (one ticker iterating profiles under a scope guard) is a source of many fixes; documented as "per-profile process assumptions are the bug class".

name: Consent-first automation suggestions
what: The agent and catalog can propose ready-to-run automations that the user accepts with one tap or dismisses forever; nothing is created automatically and the pending list is capped to avoid nagging.
how: cron/suggestions.py stores suggestions with a job_spec, dedup_key latch and status pending/accepted/dismissed; VALID_SOURCES = catalog, blueprint, usage, integration; MAX_PENDING = 5; accept calls cron.jobs.create_job with the stored spec (no second job engine). suggestion_catalog seeds curated starters (daily briefing, important-mail monitor using classify_items.py). Producers for the usage and integration sources were not found in the tree.
verevonRelevance: Matches Verevon consent and Control-decision rules; "the review proposes an automation from observed usage" is a natural extension of the learning loop.
notes: The usage source is declared (self-improvement review) but no producer was found: treat as planned.

name: Automation Blueprints: one slot schema rendered everywhere
what: A parameterized automation (daily briefing, weekday monitors) is defined once with typed slots and renders as a dashboard form, a pre-filled /blueprint command, an agent seed prompt and a docs deep link; users never type cron syntax.
how: cron/blueprint_catalog.AutomationBlueprint (key, title, category, schedule_template with {slot} placeholders, prompt_template, slots of type time/enum/text/weekdays) plus fill_blueprint that validates values into create_job kwargs. tools/blueprints.py lets any skill declare metadata.hermes.blueprint (schedule, deliver, prompt, no_agent, model, provider, enabled_toolsets) so blueprints ride the skills-hub pipeline and can be exported back to SKILL.md.
verevonRelevance: Verevon BLUEPRINT_ACTIVATION_DESIGN.md exists; the "skill that declares an automation" idea unifies skills, sharing and scheduling.

name: Cron runs keep memory but never learn (and a doc/code mismatch)
what: Scheduled runs load the profile persona and memory but skip the post-turn review fork, so automations consume memory without writing skills or notes.
how: cron/scheduler.py builds the cron agent with skip_memory=False and skip_background_review=True ("~30K tokens per event with no human in the loop"). cron/AGENTS.md still says "Cron sessions pass skip_memory=True; memory providers intentionally do not run during cron". agent_init comments also say cron agents now take the normal memory path. Session search demotes cron sessions so they do not dominate recall.
verevonRelevance: Decide explicitly for Verevon: scheduled runs should read org/user memory but write only through an approval path or not at all.
notes: Docs are stale relative to code here; code is ground truth.

name: /goal: judge-driven persistent objective (Ralph loop) with quality gates
what: A standing goal keeps the agent working across turns until an auxiliary judge decides it is done, blocked or waiting; deterministic shell gates must pass before DONE can be declared.
how: hermes_cli/goals.py: after each turn a judge (auxiliary.goal_judge, 30 s timeout, 4,096 max tokens) returns DONE / BLOCKED / WAIT / CONTINUE as JSON; failures are fail-open (continue) with auto-pause after 3 parse failures or 5 transport failures; budget DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS 20; optional completion contract (verification, constraints, stop condition), /subgoal criteria, wait barriers on background processes or sessions; gates (/goal gate add) run before the judge and a failed gate output becomes the continuation prompt (300 s timeout, 3 retries). Continuation is a normal user message so the cache stays intact; state persists in SessionDB state_meta.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Do mode could gain a judged completion loop with evidence-bearing gates rather than relying on the model to self-terminate.
notes: Adjacent to the learning facet (agent runtime) but included because it is an autonomy loop that shares the SessionDB and cache rules.

name: /loop self-paced backoff and /heartbeat idle re-entry
what: /loop re-runs a prompt or slash command on a fixed or self-paced cadence inside the session (backing off while replies do not change); /heartbeat gives a session one recurring instruction that fires only when idle and coalesces missed ticks.
how: hermes_cli/loops.py: min fixed interval 30 s, backstop 100 ticks, self-paced floor 60 s doubling to a 15 min ceiling and resetting on change, stop on a LOOP_COMPLETE line, --times, or an --until judge; state in SessionDB state_meta. hermes_cli/heartbeat.py: minimum 60 s, injected only between turns as a plain user message ("if nothing changed reply briefly"), state heartbeat:<session_id> that follows compression rotations; gateway watchers restore after restarts.
verevonRelevance: In-thread recurring wake-ups keep full conversation context, which Verevon cron (isolated runs) cannot offer.
notes: Mechanics read from module headers and docs.

name: Context budget breakdown that names memory and skills
what: The /context view breaks the window into system prompt, tools, skills, memory, MCP, subagent definitions and conversation so users and operators can see what memory and skills cost every turn.
how: agent/context_breakdown.py estimates tokens per tier from the stable prompt tier, tool schemas, the <available_skills> block and the MemoryStore snapshot blocks; zero categories are dropped except conversation (a deliberate membership rule); estimates are labelled as not tokenizer-exact and not gate authority. hermes prompt-size reports the fixed prompt footprint.
verevonRelevance: Fits the DeepSeek-style transparency goal: show users how many tokens memory, skills and instructions consume per turn.

name: Insights engine over the session database
what: A usage report aggregates sessions into tokens, cost estimates (with honest estimate labels), tool and skill usage, activity patterns and model/platform breakdowns for any number of days.
how: agent/insights.InsightsEngine(db).generate(days=30) reads sessions and messages, uses usage_pricing to estimate cost per model, counts skill_view/skill_manage calls, and renders terminal or dashboard output; sub-cent totals are shown at 4 decimals (format_cost_label).
verevonRelevance: Verevon insights_overview exists as a chat tool; learned-skill and memory usage could be added as sections.

name: Memory and skills as plain files on disk (portability versus multi-tenancy)
what: Everything learned is stored as human-readable files in the profile home (MEMORY.md, USER.md, SKILL.md trees, JSON sidecars, a pending/ staging dir, ledger and snapshots) that can be edited, backed up and moved; sessions are the only database.
how: get_hermes_home() resolves the profile root (ContextVar override); atomic writes via utils.atomic_write_text / atomic_json_write; cross-process locks via fcntl/msvcrt; hermes backup/import includes provider backup_paths(); profile distributions exclude user-owned dirs.
verevonRelevance: A cloud multi-tenant product needs a DB, but offering export/import of memory and skills as plain Markdown (and a user-visible "memory file") would match the transparency promise.
notes: Limitation: no per-user scoping inside a profile; shared group chats rely on external providers (Honcho peers, identity mapping).

name: Prompt-cache-sacred and narrow-waist doctrines as architecture rules
what: Two written invariants drive design reviews: never mutate past context, swap toolsets, reload memory or rebuild the prompt mid-conversation (compression is the only exception), and keep the core tool surface minimal because every tool is paid on every call.
how: AGENTS.md "Two invariants". Mechanisms that follow: frozen memory snapshot, api_content sidecar, system-prompt tiers, goal and heartbeat prompts as plain user messages, dispatch-side whitelists, skill index change notes, deferred tools (tool_search) and schema diets validated by A/B evals; new capability should arrive as CLI command plus skill, service-gated tool or plugin.
verevonRelevance: Worth adopting verbatim as Model Plane review rules: every feature must state its prompt-cache impact and tool-schema token cost.
notes: Most of the repo learning-efficiency design is a consequence of these two rules.

name: Hermes learning loop as a whole: strengths and weaknesses
what: The loop is consent-aware, cache-friendly, auditable and reversible, but depends on one LLM judgement per cadence with no outcome evaluation and no semantic retrieval in core.
how: Chain: nudge counters to cache-parity fork to whitelisted memory/skill tools with read-before-write and write-approval gate to ledger and usage telemetry to idle curator archive and optional consolidation to journey view with edit/delete. Retrieval chain: frozen memory snapshot + skills index (model-routed) + FTS5 session search + optional external provider prefetch.
verevonRelevance: Synthesis record: keep Verevon feedback-driven quarantine and calibration, adopt Hermes review safety (add-only unattended, read-before-write, approval staging), ledger and idle curator.
notes: Weaknesses: tiny built-in memory budget, cadence-based triggers miss one-off corrections, no user-model, no embeddings in core, review quality unevaluated, single-user profile scoping, doc drift (cron memory, search summarization).

name: Tiered injection scanning, credential-exfil guard and auto-pause for unattended runs
what: Scheduled jobs run non-interactively with auto-approved tools, so their prompts are scanned (strict for the short user prompt, narrower for the assembled prompt that includes skill bodies), a provider/base_url pair that could leak a stored key is refused, and an unrunnable job is auto-paused with an audit reason instead of re-firing forever.
how: cron/scheduler_prompt._scan_assembled_cron_prompt chooses the scanner by content: user prompt only gets the strict _scan_cron_prompt; prompts with skills or injected data get _scan_cron_skill_assembled (only unambiguous directives such as "ignore previous instructions"; command-shape patterns dropped because skill postmortems describe them; invisible Unicode sanitized rather than blocked so a false positive cannot kill a job permanently). _guard_job_credential_exfil validates the stored provider/base_url pair at run time and fails closed. _block_and_pause_job calls pause_job with paused_reason and emits an alert document.
verevonRelevance: Verevon scheduled and Do-mode runs are also unattended; scanning assembled prompts (skills, injected data) and pausing on a trip with an auditable reason are cheap controls to add before enabling tool use in scheduled runs.
notes: Motivated by issue #3968 (a malicious skill carrying an injection payload bypassed every gate under cron auto-approval).

name: Todo list as working memory that survives compaction
what: The model keeps a revisioned task list for multi-step work. After context compression the list is re-injected as a synthetic row so the plan is never lost, and UI clients can reject stale updates.
how: tools/todo_tool.TodoStore holds {id, content, status, parent} items (statuses pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled; max 256 items and 4,000 chars each) with a monotonic revision bumped on every write; one todo_list tool reads (no args) or writes (replace or merge by id). TODO_INJECTION_HEADER marks the post-compaction row so ContextCompressor and the commit path can tell it from a real user message, strip the old snapshot and re-add the current list; the store is rehydrated from history with a 512,000 char cap on forged results.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has plan mode and approved plans prepended to runs; a compaction-proof, revisioned task list would give Do mode durable working memory across tiers of compaction.
notes: Bounded caps matter because the list rides through every compaction.

name: Skills as slash commands with stacking and bundles
what: Every installed skill is a /skill-name command; up to five leading skill tokens can be stacked in one message, and YAML bundles group skills (plus a standing instruction) under a single command.
how: agent/skill_commands.py builds a per-identity (platform, home, project) command map shared by CLI and gateway, with a multi-slot cache and collision handling; leading /skill tokens are parsed until the first non-skill token, then the skill bodies are loaded into one user message with the remaining text as the instruction (MemoryManager later strips the scaffolding so providers see only the instruction). Bundles live in ~/.hermes/skill-bundles/<slug>.yaml with name, description, skills and instruction and are managed with hermes bundles.
verevonRelevance: Verevon capability-core has a command catalogue (/models, /compact) with no composer wiring; skills-as-commands and bundles give users a way to invoke learned procedures deterministically.
notes: Command-map internals were read at header level only.

name: Adapting to the user over time: corrections become task-skill rules
what: The assistant tailors itself by turning the user corrections and frustration signals ("stop doing X", "too verbose", "remember this") into rules inside the skill that governs that kind of task, so the next session starts already fixed; only cross-cutting preferences go to USER.md.
how: The skill and combined review prompts list signals that warrant action (style, tone, format, verbosity or workflow corrections; non-trivial technique; a loaded skill that proved wrong or outdated) and a "User-preference embedding" rule: the lesson lives in exactly one place, the governing skill when one exists, USER.md only when no skill owns it. Patches are applied to the skill loaded in the session first. The compaction template separately records user corrections verbatim under Errors & Fixes so they survive compaction until the review runs.
verevonRelevance: Verevon persona and custom instructions are configured by admins; learning per-task user preferences into scoped skills would personalise without growing a global memory block.
notes: Cadence-based triggering (every 10 turns or 10 tool iterations) can miss a one-off correction before the session ends; an explicit /refine or the model own skill_manage call covers the gap.
